newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Steady amid low Taiwan award.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Steady amid low Taiwan award.

text.p: Gasoline prices held steady despite the hike in crude, with Taiwan's reformate tender awarded at low levels, traders said on Wednesday.

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has bought just one 250,000 barrels of unleaded 95-octane reformate at $28.60 per barrel c-and-f April 16-30 to Keelung, Taichung, Kaohsiung or Shalung from a Swiss trader, traders said.
The tender closed March 18 and was valid for two days.
Taiwan last bought April 1-15 requirements - 250,000-barrels of each leaded and unleaded reformate - at higher levels of close to $29.00 per barrel, c-and-f.
"I don't think it is reflective of the market," a major said on the award. "If you look at Singapore, 95-octane should then be $27.50 fob."
Taiwan received ten offers for the cargo, some as high as $31.00 per barrel c-and-f, but some traders said they did not participate due to the sudden rise in crude.
"Some people are very tired by sellers going in at such numbers...leaving so much money on the table," a trader said.
Other traders saw the award however as reasonable, saying prices were heading south in April anyway as the tightness eases with refineries returning from turnarounds.
On the Singapore fob market, a European major only improved offers marginally despite overnight May Brent crude's hefty 75 cents hike to $20.25 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange.
Unleaded 97, 95 and 92-octane were respectively offered at $29.00 per barrel, $28.70 and $28.50 for 50,000-barrels lifting April 1-15 lifting.
The major later sold the 97-octane at $28.85 to a Dutch trader for April 8-12.
On Tuesday, offers were at $28.80 per barrel for 97-octane and $28.60 for 95-octane, with 92-octane traded at $28.15 lifting April 4-8.
Naphtha rose with overnight crude and fundamental support with a shosha actively buying in Japan but by late Wednesday, prices lost some of its earlier gains.
"All the bids disappeared," one trader said.
Naphtha April swaps were last quoted at $24.20/$24.60 per barel, 20 cents higher than Tuesday's quotes but losing almost 40 cents from earlier in the day. May paper traded at $24.20.
Tokyo's open-spec also lost ground to trade late Wednesday at $237 per tonne for first-half June, down from mid-afternoon quotes of $239/$240.50 but up from Tuesday's quotes at $233/$234.
Second-half May fell to $239.50/$240 from earlier quotes of $243/$244.50 but also up from Tuesday's $236.00/$237.00.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
